connections.why: Both apply systems thinking to physical processes and hazards
The carbon cycle is central to understanding climate change
Both compulsory themes use the systems and feedback model
Migration links local place change to global governance
Governance shapes how emerging economies grow and trade
Hazard vulnerability is tied to a country's development
Nutrient and water cycling sustain ecosystem function
Energy choices both drive and respond to climate change
Sampling and statistics underpin a robust investigation
Spatial data and mapping support fieldwork enquiry
A sound design enables rigorous analysis and conclusions
Data is interpreted using statistical techniques
Place studies are common human-geography NEA topics
Physical landscape systems are common NEA fieldwork topics
